extracted.intended_audience: USPTO stakeholders, patent and trademark practitioners, agency policymakers, Congress, and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, performance measures, legal/administrative rules, and strategic objectives the USPTO uses to evaluate and produce patents, trademarks, PTAB decisions, and agency performance. Includes examination criteria, performance targets, legal standards from case law, open-data/big-data initiatives, and management priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent organization examines patent applications to determine whether the claimed invention is eligible for patent protection, useful, adequately disclosed, clearly defined, and evaluates the claimed invention in comparison to a large body of technological information to determine whether it is novel and non-obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners perform administrative review of newly filed applications, publish pending applications, issue patents to successful applicants, disseminate issued patents to the public, respond to appeal briefs, and prepare preliminary PCT examination reports. Evaluation is done against existing technological information (prior art) to assess novelty and non-obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard in inter partes review (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: During inter partes review, a patent claim 'shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the patent in which it appears.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supreme Court (Cuozzo) upheld the USPTO regulation adopting broadest reasonable interpretation for claim construction in IPRs. This standard governs how PTAB judges construe claims during AIA proceedings and provides certainty to parties and adjudicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of institution decisions in IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIA provides that the agency's decision 'whether to institute an inter partes review...shall be final and non-appealable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supreme Court adopted the USPTO’s view that institution decisions are generally not subject to further court review (except in rare circumstances). This reduces litigation over institution and conserves agency resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced damages standard (post-Halo)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent infringer’s subjective willfulness may warrant enhanced damages; courts should apply a more flexible, case-by-case approach rather than the Federal Circuit’s rigid two-part test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Halo Electronics v. Pulse Electronics lowered the bar for enhanced damages under 35 U.S.C. § 284, allowing awards when there is egregious misconduct such as deliberate copying. The decision reduces the evidentiary burden required for enhanced damages compared to the prior Federal Circuit standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of high-quality patents (Enhanced Patent Quality Initiative)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality patents are 'patents that are correctly issued in compliance with all requirements of Title 35 as well as the relevant case law at the time of issuance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Enhanced Patent Quality Initiative (EPQI) comprises multiple programs (training, measurement, guidance updates, ombudsman services, interview practices) aimed at improving accuracy, clarity, and consistency of issued patents and how patent quality is measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key performance measures (Strategic Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO established 10 Strategic Plan key performance outcome measures (with supporting measures) to monitor progress implementing strategic goals; annual performance targets are developed for each measurable outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting and key measures are reported (semiannually) and visible via the USPTO performance dashboard. Examples (from Table 2) include: Average First Action Pendency (months), Average Total Pendency (months), Trademark Average First Action and Total Pendency, First Action Compliance Rate, Final Compliance Rate, Exceptional Office Action rate, and Trademark Applications Processed Electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance target achievement categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance target attainment is categorized as: Met (100% of target), Slightly below (95–99% of target), Not met (below 95% of target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are used to summarize whether key performance measures met established annual targets and are illustrated in performance tables and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark pendency targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain Trademark First Action Pendency on Average Between 2.5–3.5 Months with 12 Months Pendency (total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit Strategic Plan objective aimed at balancing timeliness and quality for trademark examination. Related performance measures include first action and total pendency values reported annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain PTAB ability to provide timely and high-quality decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) can provide timely and high-quality decisions, including meeting statutory AIA pendency requirements (e.g., 12-month pendency for trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB workload increases (AIA trials, new testimonial evidence rules) make meeting statutory timelines challenging; the USPTO monitors and addresses resourcing and process changes to preserve timeliness and decision quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data goals and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the discoverability, accessibility, and usability of public patent and trademark information through APIs, bulk data, visualization tools, and community features (the Developer Hub).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Developer Hub provides APIs to USPTO data, open-source visualization tools, and an online community to share visualizations and insights. Open data supports external value-added products, research (e.g., Cancer Moonshot Challenge), and broader innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of big data and analytics to improve patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Harness big data enterprise-wide to institutionalize, measure, and continually refine the success of patent quality initiatives, including risk management via machine learning and modeling of work products to increase quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO implemented a Big Data Roadmap, hired data scientists, built a big data reservoir, and prototypes tools for advanced analytics and business intelligence to move from 20th-century metrics to data-driven operations for improved patent and trademark quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional office outreach and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional offices serve as hubs of education, outreach, and innovation, enabling innovators to meet examiners (face-to-face or by video), learn IP basics, and use search terminals to determine novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing regional offices is intended to expand stakeholder engagement, make USPTO resources accessible nationwide, and support innovators, entrepreneurs, and small businesses across geographic regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable funding and fee management
rubrics_metrics.description: Attain and maintain full sustainable funding by pursuing access to fee collections, maintaining a prudent operating reserve, optimizing the fee structure under existing authorities, and seeking permanent fee-setting authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a user-fee–funded agency, failure to secure sustainable funding risks losing fee-payer confidence and could impair the USPTO’s ability to fulfill performance commitments; the agency conducts multiyear planning and outreach to oversight bodies to explain its funding model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of AIA trial practice changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement AIA trial practice provisions, including changes that allow patent owners to submit new testimonial evidence during PTAB trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practice changes affect PTAB workload and trial procedures; USPTO monitors impacts on pendency and process fairness and reports how PTAB addresses resulting challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and transparency of patent application lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform the patent process functions: administrative review of newly filed applications, publishing pending applications, issuing patents to successful applicants, and disseminating issued patents to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural requirements support public disclosure (Progress Clause) and ensure the patent system balances exclusive rights with public knowledge to foster innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examination process and registrability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining attorneys determine registrability under the Trademark Act of 1946 by searching databases for confusingly similar marks, preparing applicant correspondence, approving applications for publication for opposition, and examining statements of use in Intent-to-Use applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trademark organization registers marks that meet statutory requirements and measures quality via compliance rates and exceptional office action rates reported in performance tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce quality, hiring, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruiting and retaining the highest quality employees, providing training (e.g., classes for new examiners), and maintaining a diverse and engaged workforce to accomplish agency mission and performance goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workforce metrics (staff counts, examiner classes, regional hiring) and training standards are part of the EPQI and broader management goals to ensure consistent examination quality and organizational excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Performance Framework and balanced scorecard
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive Strategic Performance Framework including a balanced scorecard, action plans for initiatives, and semiannual reporting to leadership to guide and monitor implementation of objectives and performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each business unit prepares action plans, documents results semiannually, and reports to the Director and executive staff; supporting measures are published online in the performance dashboard.
